assumptions.reason: Spec requires 'full available capital' per trade; a 1% buffer is retained so the order isn't rejected due to the 0.1% commission and the gap between the signal bar's close and the actual next-bar fill price.

assumptions.choice: Size is computed using the current (signal) bar's close price rather than the fill price
assumptions.reason: Backtrader executes market orders on the following bar; the actual fill price is unknown at submission time, so the last known close is the closest literal basis.

assumptions.choice: A protective bt.Order.Stop is submitted immediately after the entry order completes, sized to the entry's filled size, at entry_price * (1 - 2%) for longs / entry_price * (1 + 2%) for shorts
assumptions.reason: Spec states a 2% stop from entry price but not an order type; a stop-market order triggered off the actual fill price is the standard literal implementation.

assumptions.choice: The live stop order is cancelled at the moment the day-based exit (Friday for longs, Monday for shorts) fires self.close()
assumptions.reason: Spec doesn't address the interplay between the stop and the day-based exit; cancelling avoids a stale stop order acting on a position that scheduled exit has already closed.

assumptions.choice: Monday/Friday day-of-week conditions are re-checked on every 15-minute bar of that day, so the action fires on the first qualifying intraday bar
assumptions.reason: Spec's rules are day-level but the feed is intraday and silent on time-of-day; checking every bar of the named day is the closest literal reading.

assumptions.choice: On Friday, an open long is closed via self.close() first; a new short can only be entered once flat (a subsequent bar), so entry and exit signals never stack in the same order batch
assumptions.reason: Canonical default of holding at most one position at a time; spec doesn't explicitly address a Friday bar satisfying both the long-exit and short-entry conditions simultaneously.
